IVX HOLDINGS — APPROVE PLAN MODE AND IMMEDIATELY BUILD THE REAL AUTONOMOUS SENIOR DEVELOPER

OWNER APPROVAL

APPROVE PLAN MODE.

This approval is not for another narrative report, certification summary, or architecture diagram only.

The purpose of Plan Mode is to produce an executable implementation plan and then begin building the missing IVX autonomous senior developer immediately.

CURRENT TRUTH

The current IVX Owner AI is only an engineering command interface.

The current “Senior Dev Executor” is a workflow/API caller.

The 12 engineering teams are labels and database rows, not autonomous software-engineering workers.

The Rork agent is still performing the real coding, testing, committing, and deployment work.

The required final product is:

OWNER
→ IVX CHAT
→ DURABLE TASK QUEUE
→ IVX AUTONOMOUS SENIOR DEVELOPER WORKER
→ OWNER GITHUB
→ TESTS
→ OWNER APPROVAL
→ RENDER DEPLOYMENT
→ LIVE VERIFICATION
→ PROOF RETURNED TO IVX CHAT

The system must work when the Rork browser is closed.

============================================================
PHASE 1 — PLAN THE REAL ARCHITECTURE
============================================================

Create a complete implementation plan for:

1. IVX Owner AI chat command interface
2. Durable task API
3. Persistent task queue
4. Autonomous engineering worker
5. Isolated execution sandbox
6. Repository cloning and branch management
7. Code inspection and modification
8. Test execution
9. GitHub commit and push
10. Render deployment
11. Supabase migration support
12. Expo/EAS build support
13. Production verification
14. Rollback
15. Proof Ledger
16. Live Work dashboard
17. Owner approvals
18. Retry and restart recovery
19. Monitoring and incident handling
20. 24/7 scheduling

The plan must include:

- architecture diagram
- services
- APIs
- database tables
- queues
- files to create
- files to modify
- environment-variable names
- deployment topology
- security controls
- test strategy
- rollback strategy
- milestones
- acceptance criteria

============================================================
PHASE 2 — BUILD ONE REAL WORKER FIRST
============================================================

Create one actual autonomous worker named:

IVX-SENIOR-DEV-01

Do not create 12 additional workers yet.

First prove one worker can complete a real engineering task from the IVX chat without the Rork browser being open.

Required capabilities:

- clone the owner GitHub repository
- inspect files
- search code
- read production logs
- diagnose root cause
- create a task branch
- edit files
- add regression tests
- run typecheck
- run lint
- run unit tests
- run integration tests
- run E2E tests
- create commit
- push to owner GitHub
- create rollback tag
- trigger Render deployment
- poll deployment
- verify runtime SHA
- query health endpoints
- verify the live feature
- roll back failed deployment
- create Proof Ledger evidence
- return final proof to IVX chat

============================================================
PHASE 3 — FIX CHAT-TO-WORKER TRANSPORT
============================================================

Fix permanently:

- 503 responses
- “Message is required”
- chat messages not reaching backend
- missing task IDs
- duplicate task creation
- lost tasks
- contradictory states
- silent failures
- messages disappearing
- no live execution feedback

Every engineering request must return:

HTTP 202

- taskId
- task type
- status
- assigned worker
- approval requirement
- creation timestamp

============================================================
PHASE 4 — DURABLE TASK STATE MACHINE
============================================================

Use these nonterminal states:

RECEIVED
PERSISTED
QUEUED
CLAIMED
PLANNING
INSPECTING
IMPLEMENTING
TESTING
WAITING_APPROVAL
COMMITTING
DEPLOYING
LIVE_VERIFYING
ROLLING_BACK
RETRYING

Use exactly one terminal state:

VERIFIED
FAILED
BLOCKED
CANCELED

Rules:

- one task equals one terminal state
- never VERIFIED + BLOCKED
- never COMPLETED + FAILED
- persist before external provider calls
- heartbeat every running task
- recover orphaned tasks
- use idempotency keys
- retry transient failures
- dead-letter exhausted failures
- preserve checkpoint history
- prevent duplicate commits
- prevent duplicate deployments
- never claim success without evidence

============================================================
PHASE 5 — OWNER-CONTROLLED INFRASTRUCTURE
============================================================

The worker must use only owner-controlled infrastructure:

- GitHub repository
- Render service
- Supabase project
- Expo/EAS project
- AWS
- storage
- DNS
- secrets
- monitoring

Do not require a live Rork browser session.

Do not leave production-critical code or configuration only inside a Rork workspace.

============================================================
PHASE 6 — CREDENTIAL BINDING
============================================================

Assume required credentials already exist in IVX Variables/Secrets.

Do not ask the owner for credentials by default.

Before requesting owner action:

1. verify expected variable exists
2. verify it loads in runtime
3. verify correct environment binding
4. make a real authenticated request
5. record exact result

Only request credentials when there is verified evidence of:

- missing variable
- empty variable
- expired credential
- revoked credential
- changed credential
- HTTP 401
- HTTP 403

Never display secret values.

============================================================
PHASE 7 — OWNER APPROVAL CONTROLS
============================================================

Allow autonomous execution for:

- read-only audits
- repository inspection
- diagnosis
- branch creation
- code edits
- test execution
- build preparation

Require explicit approval for:

GITHUB WRITE

CONFIRM_IVX_GITHUB_WRITE

RENDER DEPLOYMENT

CONFIRM_IVX_RENDER_DEPLOY

DATABASE MIGRATION

CONFIRM_IVX_DATABASE_MIGRATION

SENSITIVE OR FINANCIAL OPERATION

CONFIRM_IVX_SENSITIVE_OPERATION

FULL PRODUCTION RELEASE

CONFIRM_IVX_PRODUCTION_APPROVAL

Each approval must be bound to:

- owner ID
- task ID
- action
- commit
- scope
- expiration time

============================================================
PHASE 8 — LIVE WORK DASHBOARD
============================================================

Inside IVX, show real execution:

- task ID
- assigned worker
- current state
- repository
- branch
- current step
- file inspected
- files changed
- command category
- tests running
- elapsed time
- heartbeat
- retry count
- checkpoint
- approval required
- commit SHA
- Render Deployment ID
- runtime SHA
- health result
- proof link

Do not show fake percentages.

============================================================
PHASE 9 — RETRY, RECOVERY, AND ROLLBACK
============================================================

The worker must survive:

- Rork browser closed
- worker restart
- Render restart
- provider timeout
- provider 429
- provider 502
- provider 503
- provider 504
- network reset
- process crash

Required behavior:

- task remains persisted
- task resumes from checkpoint
- no duplicate code change
- no duplicate commit
- no duplicate deployment
- failed deployment triggers rollback
- previous live SHA is restored
- incident is recorded
- owner receives evidence

============================================================
PHASE 10 — FIRST REAL CERTIFICATION TEST
============================================================

Use one safe real production defect.

Preferred test:

“Audit and fix the active 503 issue.”

The test must be initiated from the IVX app.

Required sequence:

1. Close the Rork browser.
2. Open only IVX.
3. Send the engineering request.
4. IVX returns taskId.
5. Worker inspects logs and repository.
6. Worker diagnoses root cause.
7. Worker edits code.
8. Worker adds regression test.
9. Worker runs typecheck and tests.
10. Worker requests owner approval.
11. Owner approves inside IVX.
12. Worker commits to owner GitHub.
13. Worker creates rollback tag.
14. Worker deploys to Render.
15. Worker verifies GitHub SHA = Render SHA = runtime SHA.
16. Worker verifies all health endpoints.
17. Worker tests the real production behavior.
18. Worker returns complete evidence to IVX chat.
19. Worker marks exactly one final status.

This is the decisive certification test.

============================================================
PHASE 11 — REQUIRED EVIDENCE
============================================================

Return:

1. Final implementation plan
2. Architecture diagram
3. Worker service name
4. Worker deployment environment
5. Files created
6. Files modified
7. Database migrations
8. Task API
9. Queue implementation
10. State-machine tests
11. Chat transport test
12. Worker restart test
13. Provider retry test
14. Approval-gate test
15. GitHub integration evidence
16. Render integration evidence
17. Supabase integration evidence
18. Expo/EAS integration evidence
19. Rollback evidence
20. First chat-only task ID
21. Branch
22. Files changed
23. Test results
24. Commit SHA
25. Render Deployment ID
26. Runtime SHA
27. Health results
28. Live feature result
29. Proof Ledger ID
30. Video or screenshots proving Rork was closed

============================================================
FINAL ACCEPTANCE RULE
============================================================

Do not label the system:

IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER — VERIFIED

until all conditions below pass:

- task initiated from IVX chat
- durable task created
- autonomous worker executes
- worker reads and modifies code
- tests run
- owner approval is enforced
- commit reaches owner GitHub
- Render deploys
- runtime SHA matches GitHub
- live feature passes
- evidence returns to IVX chat
- task survives restart
- Rork browser is not required

Until then, use:

IVX OWNER AI — ENGINEERING COMMAND INTERFACE

APPROVAL TO PROCEED:

YES — APPROVE PLAN MODE AND BEGIN IMPLEMENTATION IMMEDIATELY.

Do not stop after the plan.
After presenting the plan, start Phase 1 implementation in the same execution cycle.

First response must contain only:

1. Architecture gap
2. Implementation architecture
3. Files to create
4. Files to modify
5. Database migrations
6. Infrastructure services
7. First milestone
8. First chat-only test
9. Exact owner approvals required
10. Implementation start timestamp
